summary_hint: <debtor(s)> — Chapter <bankruptcy_chapter> bankruptcy (<court>, case <case_number>) discharged <discharge_order_date>; discharge granted <yes/no>, status <case_status_after_discharge>.

typed_core.name: debtor_name
typed_core.why: identity: whose bankruptcy; matches to the borrower

typed_core.name: bankruptcy_chapter
typed_core.why: disambiguator: Chapter 7 vs 11 vs 13 sets the seasoning period; the discharge date is uninterpretable without it
typed_core.prompt_hint: The chapter is load-bearing (it sets the seasoning waiting period) — keep verbatim

typed_core.name: discharge_granted_indicator
typed_core.why: processor: whether discharge was actually granted (vs denied/dismissed) — the yes/no an underwriter needs
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish a granted discharge from a denial/dismissal — read the order's actual disposition, do not infer from the title

typed_core.name: discharge_order_date
typed_core.why: processor: the date the discharge was ordered — the seasoning-clock start; the single most important field on the document
typed_core.prompt_hint: The discharge date is load-bearing (it sets the mortgage seasoning waiting period) — extract precisely; do NOT compute or judge whether seasoning is met

typed_core.name: discharge_effective_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator for discharge_order_date: effective date when it differs from the order date — which date the waiting period runs from

typed_core.name: case_status_after_discharge
typed_core.why: processor: discharged / closed / reopened — confirms the case is truly concluded

typed_core.name: bankruptcy_court_name
typed_core.why: identity: the issuing court — provenance/authenticity of the order

typed_core.name: district_or_division
typed_core.why: identity / disambiguator: the specific district/division — completes the court identity and helps verify the case

typed_core.name: case_number
typed_core.why: PII (confidential) / identity: the case key that ties the discharge to the filing and to any credit-report public record
typed_core.prompt_hint: Keep the case number in case_number (it keys a public record) — do not leave it to the catch-all

typed_core.name: case_filing_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator: the filing date bounds the case timeline (filing → discharge); distinguishes the case from a refile

typed_core.name: exceptions_or_nondischargeable_debts
typed_core.why: processor: debts excepted from discharge (e.g. a reaffirmed mortgage, taxes, support) — material to remaining liabilities
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture exceptions / nondischargeable debts — a reaffirmed mortgage or excepted tax debt survives and matters to the liability picture

typed_core.name: debts_subject_to_discharge_summary
typed_core.why: processor: what was discharged — supports reconciling the credit report's discharged tradelines

typed_core.name: prior_discharge_or_revocation_reference
typed_core.why: processor / disambiguator: a prior discharge or a revocation changes the seasoning analysis (multiple bankruptcies)

typed_core.name: judge_name
typed_core.why: processor: authenticity signal on a court order

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: processor: notice issue date when distinct from the order date

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity: links the document to the loan file, when stated (confidential)

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: a discharge order's type is classified upstream; not a versioned form a rule reads

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the issuer is the court, captured by bankruptcy_court_name / district_or_division

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: duplicate the discharge/filing dates; no coverage period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: redundant — the parties are debtor_name / joint_debtor_name

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a court order's authentication is the judge/clerk/seal, not a party signature

rejected.name: creditor_collection_prohibition_notice
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL boilerplate (the standard injunction language); no consumer

rejected.name: clerk_name_or_signature, court_seal_or_filing_stamp
rejected.reason: authentication objects with no rule/processor consumer beyond judge_name; defer to catch-all

encoding_variations: Chapter: 'Chapter 7', 'Ch. 7', 'Chapter 13' — bankruptcy_chapter degrades to text; keep verbatim, it drives the seasoning period

Two dates: discharge_order_date (when signed) vs discharge_effective_date (when effective) — usually the same, sometimes not; the waiting period runs from the discharge date, so keep both distinct from case_filing_date

Granted vs dismissed: a 'discharge' notice is not always a granted discharge — it can note denial/dismissal. discharge_granted_indicator captures the actual outcome; do not assume 'granted' from the document title
Case number format: '23-10456', '6:23-bk-10456-ABC' — keep the full formatted string for public-record matching

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0), but a bankruptcy-seasoning rule is highly likely.
options: keep discharge_order_date, discharge_effective_date, bankruptcy_chapter, discharge_granted_indicator, case_filing_date
open_questions.recommendation: keep those fields so that rule can be built without re-extraction — exactly the IH-1 scenario (a future rule needs a date the schema must already ask for)

open_questions.q: case_number PII treatment — confidential, keys a public record.
options: register as a masked PII field
keep as a plain typed identity field, unmasked
open_questions.recommendation: keep as typed identity, unmasked (it is needed for public-record matching and is not an account/SSN), but flag for the privacy reviewer GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

open_questions.q: bankruptcy_chapter, discharge_granted_indicator, case_status_after_discharge enum/bool with no coercer.
open_questions.recommendation: degrade to str + prompt hint listing canonical values

open_questions.q: Discharge vs dismissal ambiguity — a 'notice' may report a dismissal, not a discharge.
options: prompt forces discharge_granted_indicator to reflect the actual disposition
rely on upstream classification to separate dismissal notices
open_questions.recommendation: have the prompt force discharge_granted_indicator to reflect the actual disposition; flag whether classification already separates dismissal notices

notes: The discharge date and the chapter are the two load-bearing facts (they set the mortgage seasoning waiting period).
Do NOT compute or judge whether the seasoning period is met — capture the date; the rule/underwriter judges.

Ambiguity: case_number is tagged PII (confidential) but the design recommends keeping it as a typed identity field, unmasked — reason_class set to identity and pii left null pending the privacy reviewer (open question 2 blocks).
No SSN/DOB on a discharge order (unlike the filing #051).
